comments.note: MainContentViewModel.OnEditMovieRequested is async void (required for event handler). Unhandled exceptions from GetByIdAsync are swallowed by the async-void boundary after the catch block. The logger call inside the catch ensures errors are observable, but callers have no way to await or propagate the failure. This is an accepted pattern for event-driven async operations, but worth noting.

MoviesListViewModel: the old EditMovieAsync() static stub (marked 'No-op in M4') was replaced with OpenEditorForSelectedMovie(). If any future milestone resurrects a separate EditMovie concept distinct from OpenEditorForSelectedMovie, the historical intent of the original stub should be reviewed against the WP plan.

MainContentViewModel.OnEditorCloseRequested does not guard against concurrent editor opens (e.g., if a library refresh transitions away from MovieEditor and then a second editor is opened). The CloseRequested handler from the orphaned first editor will still fire and call CloseSubView() + LoadAsync unexpectedly. Low likelihood in practice, but worth tracking as a future robustness improvement.

comments.note: Context menu in MoviesListView.axaml uses {ReflectionBinding} for all items. This is the correct Avalonia pattern (ContextMenu lives outside the visual tree), but it means the binding path is validated only at runtime. No headless test covers menu rendering or command binding resolution.

OnEditMovieRequested is async void; unhandled exceptions after the try/catch boundary are silently swallowed. The catch block logs, but a repository exception mid-navigation (e.g., between GetByIdAsync and setting CurrentPage) would only be observable via the logger. Accepted pattern for event-driven async, but worth tracking.

comments.note: MainContentViewModel.OnEditorCloseRequested uses .ContinueWith(OnlyOnFaulted) to log LoadAsync failures — this is the better pattern. The older call site in OnRefreshStateChanged fires MoviesListVm.LoadAsync with a bare _ = without the same fault logging. Not introduced in this WP, but the inconsistency is worth tracking.

OnEditMovieRequested: exceptions thrown after the try/catch block (factory call, event subscription, property assignments) are technically swallowed by the async-void boundary. The catch covers the riskiest operation (DB fetch). Developer and QA both acknowledged this as accepted pattern for event-driven async. Low risk given the remaining code paths have no expected failure modes.

OnEditorCloseRequested lacks a CurrentPage guard. If a library refresh transitions CurrentPage away from MovieEditor (e.g. to RefreshOverlay) before the editor's CloseRequested fires, OnEditorCloseRequested will call CloseSubView() and interrupt the refresh. The Developer flagged this; it is low-likelihood in M6 but should be addressed before production polish.
